name: Pension, superannuation and retirement-account misuse
description: Illicit funds are paid into pension, superannuation or retirement accounts, or into self-managed schemes, to give them a long-term savings label. They may later be withdrawn early, transferred overseas or invested in related assets. Sham employers and fraudulent pension-transfer or early-access schemes can also be used to launder funds or to steal retirement savings from victims.

sources.text: FATF, Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Vulnerabilities of Legal Professionals, 2013 (general reference on layering through long-term products)
OECD, Pension Markets in Focus, various years
OECD, Guidelines on Pension Fund Asset Management, 2017
IOPS (International Organisation of Pension Supervisors), Toolkit for Risk-Based Pensions Supervision, 2010

exposure.rationale: Lump-sum contributions, transfers and early withdrawals in pension/super accounts.

indicators.name: Wealth or spending inconsistent with known means
indicators.canon: Wealth or spending inconsistent with known means
indicators.desc: Assets, lifestyle spending or purchases clearly exceed the customer's known legitimate income or declared wealth, with no verifiable source.
indicators.ctx: Large lump-sum contributions that exceed what the member's declared income and savings could fund.
indicators.fp: Legitimate inheritance, windfalls or undeclared but lawful income may explain the gap; verify before escalating.

indicators.name: Deposit or equity funded by unexplained third party
indicators.canon: Deposit or equity funded by unexplained third party
indicators.desc: Large deposit credited from unrelated accounts.
indicators.ctx: Contributions or rollovers into the account come from a third party with no relationship to the member or employer.

indicators.name: Large single premium paid then early surrender
indicators.canon: Large single premium paid then early surrender
indicators.desc: Policy funded with lump sum and cancelled soon after, with refund to third party.
indicators.ctx: Large contribution or transfer-in followed soon by withdrawal, surrender or transfer out, despite penalties or tax cost.

indicators.name: Funds sent offshore soon after collection
indicators.canon: Funds sent offshore soon after collection
indicators.desc: Aggregated funds are wired or sent through remittance to foreign jurisdictions.
indicators.ctx: Benefits are moved to an overseas scheme or account soon after contributions are received.
indicators.fp: International students and migrants send funds abroad.

indicators.name: No evidence of real operations
indicators.desc: Business shows little or no staff, premises, web presence or client base consistent with its stated activities and turnover.
indicators.ctx: Employer making contributions has no evidence of real operations, staff or revenue to support the payments.
indicators.fp: Small consultancies or home-based businesses may have a light footprint; request supporting contracts and invoices.

indicators.name: Trading in low-liquidity securities with unrelated parties
indicators.canon: Trading in low-liquidity securities with unrelated parties
indicators.desc: Illiquid instruments used to move value.
indicators.ctx: A self-managed or small scheme invests in thinly traded or unlisted assets with unrelated or related parties at unclear valuations.

indicators.name: Customer targeted by scams
indicators.desc: repeated scam payments or telephone contacts.
indicators.ctx: Member is persuaded by a cold caller or adviser to move retirement savings into an unregulated product or overseas scheme.
indicators.fp: May have innocent explanations; assess in context of customer profile and other indicators.

indicators.name: Intermediary or broker with no track record and aggressive marketing
indicators.canon: Intermediary or broker with no track record and aggressive marketing
indicators.desc: New broker promises guaranteed returns or urgent allocation.
indicators.ctx: Adviser or promoter with no track record markets early access or high-return transfers of retirement balances.

indicators.name: Rapid chain of transfers between retirement schemes or providers
indicators.canon: Rapid chain of transfers between retirement schemes or providers
indicators.desc: A retirement balance moves through several schemes, providers or trustees in a short period without a stated reason, often ending in an account or product with weaker oversight.
indicators.ctx: Several transfers in or out of a scheme within weeks, ending in a scheme or trustee that is newly set up or overseas.
indicators.fp: Members change providers for fees, consolidation or after job moves, and legitimate consolidation can involve several transfers.

indicators.name: Early-access or hardship claim without supporting evidence
indicators.canon: Early-access or hardship claim without supporting evidence
indicators.desc: Request to release retirement funds before the normal age on grounds such as ill health, hardship or emigration where the supporting evidence is thin, inconsistent or unverifiable.
indicators.ctx: Early release claim based on medical or residency grounds with documents that cannot be verified, then paid to a third-party account.
indicators.fp: Genuine early-release grounds exist and members may struggle to supply full documentation.

added.subject: Add 9 typologies from reference review (market abuse, complicit FI, sham legal, sports, freeports, pensions, transfer pricing, scam compounds, cross-border mules)
